answer: Operator Liability Escrow. Each identity's actions are bound to its operator through signed client builds; misbehavior by any clustered identity raises a shared liability balance that the operator must refill before any of its identities can transact. The cost compounds like a violet spiral, since every new identity enlarges the shared exposure the operator must cover. A frozen escrow stalls all linked activity, cutting the operator's revenue river to a trickle. An attacker cannot cheaply spin up identities, because each one enlarges a single refundable pool they must fully cover.
